text:
maria: ran the load-gauntlet (replay vs synthetic) with the new kernel-selector heuristics + KV warmup changes. posting quick summary and logs here.
ken: nice, top-level conclusions first?
jules: curious about p99 tails and how batching changed.
maria: TL;DR: replay and synth diverged for long-context tails; kernel route favors the 'fallback' kernels more under synth because of skewed seq-lens. KV warmup reduced cold p50 by ~18% on replay but didn't help synth.
ken: can you paste the key numbers?
maria: pasted raw perf snippet below (run id: gauntlet-2026-05-02-048):
```
# replay baseline -> new-heuristic (q4_0, speculative=off)
model: redwood-7b
load: 200 rps steady, 5% bursts
replay baseline p50/p95/p99: 32ms / 120ms / 310ms
replay new-heur p50/p95/p99: 26ms / 110ms / 290ms
synthetic baseline p50/p95/p99: 20ms / 75ms / 230ms
synthetic new-heur p50/p95/p99: 22ms / 98ms / 370ms
mem stable, kernel-switch count increased x1.7 on synth (more fallback kernels).
```
maria: note the synth p99 regressed despite p50 moving slightly up. pattern: more short-seq traffic in synth triggered a kernel-profile that optimizes for tiny prefixes but loses on tails.
tal: interesting — did you record kernel-tag usage?
maria: yes. kernel tags: fast-attn-32 (primary), fallback-attn (dense), qkernel-8 (quant). On synth, fallback-attn accounted for 42% of inferences after route thresholds; on replay it was 18%.
ken: is that due to length histogram mismatch?
maria: exactly. replay has heavy long-context tails -> more KV hits and sustained kv-cache, so primary kernel is better. synth had many short queries and cold-start patterns, pushing selector to low-overhead kernels that don't play well with long decoding.
jules: OK. What about batching heuristics? max_batch_ms and batch_size interplay?
maria: tested three configs: baseline (max_batch_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=1024), relaxed (max_batch_ms=12), adaptive (flush on p50 target 40ms). Results: adaptive preserved replay p99 while keeping cost ~5% lower. Relaxed reduced p50 but spiked p99 on synth.
ken: so adaptive looks promising. can we tie adaptive flush to route/kind? e.g., for fallback-attn reduce wait time?
maria: yes, we can per-kernel policies. prototype config:
```json
{"kernel_policy": {"fast-attn-32": {"max_batch_ms": 12}, "fallback-attn": {"max_batch_ms": 6}}
```
works decently in sim.
perf-bot: CI run gauntlet-2026-05-02-048: 24 tests passed, 3 flaky tests (sampling), 1 regression alert (synth p99 > baseline + 40ms).
ops-bot: deploy note: rolled the selector tweak to staging-heat for canary at 10% traffic. No errors in 30m.
tal: what about KV cache warmup heuristics? we tuned prefix caching to keep last 32 tokens vs dynamic. effects?
maria: current warmup: proactive preload for known long-doc routes (TTL 300s). That cut replay cold-starts a lot. On synth it increased memory churn without benefit. Suggest: keep proactive for routes with median >256 tokens, otherwise rely on on-demand warming.
ken: quantization profiles? did you run q4_0 vs q8_0?
maria: ran q4_0 and q8_0 on replay baseline. q4_0 reduced cost 28% but increased tail variance slightly; q8_0 reduces cost 18% with negligible tail impact. For some routes with heavy generation, q8_0 + speculative decoding offered the best cost/latency tradeoff.
jules: details on speculative config?
maria: speculative decode: two-step speculative with topk=3 shadow decode on q4_0; if top1 mismatch confidence < 0.01 fallback to full decode. In practice: hit-rate ~82% on short flows, 65% on longer ones. Latency wins mostly on short/median.
ken: regression gating strategy? Do we block rollouts based on tail regressions?
maria: propose gate: block if replay p99 increases > 20% AND synth p99 increases > 30% OR if absolute p99 delta > 50ms. The double-check (replay + synth) avoids blocking changes that only affect one traffic shape.
tal: agree. also add a cost delta check (if cost drops > 12% but p99 regresses less than thresholds, allow with monitored rollout).
jules: can you add a replay-to-synth normalization to make apples-to-apples? like sample-weighting or synthetic biasing to match length histogram.
maria: yes: two approaches we ran: 1) length-matched synthetic: resample synthetic queries to match replay length histogram; 2) weighted metrics: compute p99 by reweighting synth samples to replay distribution. Both narrow the delta; prefer weighting for CI speed.
ken: what action items?
maria: short list: 1) adopt adaptive batching prototype and per-kernel max_batch_ms (PR ready), 2) add per-route proactive-KV policy (by median length) (draft policy), 3) add regression-gate rule + cost-exception clause (docs), 4) add synth->replay reweighting in gauntlet reports (small change), 5) run extended canary with q8_0 + speculative for 48h on staging.
jules: I'll own (1) and (4).
tal: I'll take (2).
ken: I'll draft gate docs (3) and schedule canary (5) with ops.
ops-bot: scheduled canary (q8_0-spec) start 2026-05-03T03:00Z -> 48h, traffic 15% -> notify #incidents on anomaly.
perf-bot: note: attach full CSV reports to the gauntlet run object (link: https://ci.internal/gauntlet/gauntlet-2026-05-02-048).
maria: thanks team. follow-ups in the PRs and I'll post the full CSV and kernel-tag breakdown later today. :thumbsup:
